title: Pixels over Symbols: Sensory Realism Improves Behavioral Alignment in Models of Cognition
summary: Naturalistic visual inputs make trained sequential models more behaviorally consistent with human cognition than abstract inputs, with a measured gap across tasks and architectures.
ai_technology: Sequential models trained on naturalistic and abstract visual inputs
organization: McGill University; Mila, Université de Montréal

evidence.tested: Naturalistic visual inputs make trained sequential models more behaviorally consistent with human cognition than abstract inputs, with a measured gap across tasks and architectures.
evidence.unknown: The reported behavioral alignment is measured on the evaluated tasks and architectures; it does not establish a human cognitive mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: Sequential models trained on naturalistic and abstract visual inputs is used in the reported analysis or evaluation.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
